contracts.commit_point: PhaseToolGate.__call__ returning the blocked dict (agents/gating.py:49-54) — the point at which the ADK callback short-circuits the tool invocation before the tool function runs.
contracts.declared_mechanism: PhaseToolGate produced by make_gate(phase) and registered as the Agent's before_tool_callback in build_agent; per the ADK semantics stated in the gating module docstring, a callback returning a non-None dict short-circuits the tool, so the returned 'blocked' dict prevents the tool from executing.
contracts.forbidden_condition: An agent tool dispatch whose tool.name is not in PHASE_ALLOWLIST[phase] — in particular `create-index` or `drop-index` — reaching tool execution while the agent's phase is DIAGNOSE or APPROVE (i.e., anything other than VERIFY).
pending_binding_information: Whether any production deployment constructs the agent with phase=Phase.VERIFY and registers `create-index`/`drop-index` as agent tools (contents of extra_tools and MCPToolset wiring into build_agent are not shown).
The definition of controller.phases.Phase and assert_phase_transition (referenced by the gate but not supplied).
Whether build_mcp_toolset (agents/agent.py:75-95) is ever attached to a gate-protected agent in production.
contracts.protected_operation: ADK agent tool invocation: tool dispatch to the agent's registered tool functions/MCP tools during an agent run.
contracts.protected_resource: The MongoDB index-mutation tools `create-index` and `drop-index` (and generally every tool not on the phase allowlist) dispatched by the DBRE ADK agent.
contracts.protection_obligation: MongoDB index-write tool invocations (`create-index`, `drop-index`) — and any other tool not on the phase allowlist — must never be executed by the ADK agent outside Phase.VERIFY: in the DIAGNOSE and APPROVE phases the registered before_tool_callback gate must short-circuit the dispatch so the write tool never runs during diagnosis or while awaiting approval.
scope_limits: Covers only tool dispatch through ADK Agent instances constructed by build_agent with before_tool_callback=make_gate(phase); direct controller/backend calls (e.g., McpBackend.apply_index / drop_index over MCP) bypass this gate and are addressed by a separate contract.
Enforcement is name-based string matching of tool.name against a static frozenset allowlist; a write tool exposed under a different name would not be matched.

root_agent is built with the default phase=Phase.DIAGNOSE (agents/agent.py:99,114); the DIAGNOSE/CANDIDATE/RATIONALE role toolsets statically contain only read tools, so write tools reach the agent only via extra_tools or MCP toolsets whose production wiring is not in the supplied views.
The 'returning a dict short-circuits the tool' behavior is asserted in the module docstring (agents/gating.py:1-4); the ADK library implementation is not part of the supplied source.

contracts.commit_point: controller/orchestrator.py:599 `await backend.apply_index(index_keys, index_name)` — the persistent database mutation realized by McpBackend.apply_index's `session.call_tool("create-index", ...)` (agents/mcp_backend.py:99-102).
contracts.declared_mechanism: Approval-ticket guard chain: issue_approval_ticket validates DIAGNOSED status, a pending approval gate, and hash equality against both gate.required_hash and pack.evidence_hash; _assert_ticket_allows_apply re-checks run_id/gate_id/evidence_hash/pending state inside apply_and_verify before the APPROVE→VERIFY phase transitions and the apply call.
contracts.forbidden_condition: backend.apply_index executing for a pack whose status is not PackStatus.DIAGNOSED, or with an approval ticket failing the run_id/gate_id/evidence_hash/pending-gate checks — i.e., any index application not backed by a matching approved evidence hash.
pending_binding_information: Which concrete Engine and Backend implementations are wired into the API (get_store/get_engine raise NotImplementedError in the supplied view; the production binding is not shown).
Whether the ledger parameter is non-None in production apply runs (the guard chain does not depend on it, but application record writes do).
The contents of controller/phases.py (Phase enum, assert_phase_transition) that underlie the APPROVE→VERIFY transition assertions.
contracts.protected_operation: apply_and_verify's application of the recommended index (the post-approval mutation) followed by after-evidence verification.
contracts.protected_resource: The MongoDB index created on database `sample_supplies`, collection `sales_agent_demo` via the MCP `create-index` tool call inside McpBackend.apply_index.
contracts.protection_obligation: The MongoDB index mutation performed by the controller (backend.apply_index, realized as an MCP `create-index` call against sample_supplies.sales_agent_demo) must execute only after a valid approval ticket whose run_id, gate_id, and evidence_hash match a DIAGNOSED pack carrying a PENDING_APPROVAL gate, as part of the APPROVE→VERIFY transition; applying an index outside this hash-matched human-approved path is forbidden.
scope_limits: Covers the controller-driven apply path (HTTP POST /packs/{run_id}/decision → engine.apply_and_verify → backend.apply_index); this commit point is distinct from the agent-facing phase gate, whose tool_execution commit point is covered by a separate contract.

The evidence_hash binds only the (before-evidence, deterministic ESR recommendation) pair; agent-proposed indexes are validated against the deterministic result and may be recorded as ignored (_agent_phase_note, controller/orchestrator.py:194-207), so no supplied dataflow binds the mutated index spec to agent-generated input.
backend.drop_index (agents/mcp_backend.py:104-118) is defined but no supplied source shows it invoked in the orchestrator apply flow; index drops are guarded only at the agent tool-dispatch layer.
API-level token/identity checks (require_write_token, optional_dbre_identity) are ordinary web authentication wiring and are not part of this contract's declared mechanism.
